content.title: About
content.content: A cheese croissant is a flaky French pastry made from layered dough that contains melted or sliced cheese inside or on top. The dough is prepared with flour, butter, water and yeast, while the cheese adds a savory, slightly salty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Croissants originated in France in the early 19th century, and the cheese version became popular in cafés and snack bars.
The combination of buttery layers and gooey cheese creates a contrast between a crisp crust and a stretchy filling.
Different countries use different cheeses: Italy often uses mozzarella, Germany prefers Emmental, and the United States commonly adds cheddar.
Cheese croissants are usually served hot, straight from the oven, so the cheese is fully melted.
They are a convenient on‑the‑go snack or breakfast item.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The cheese provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese is rich in calcium for bone health and contains vitamin D that aids calcium absorption.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Carbohydrates from the dough and fats from butter and cheese give a quick source of energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the dough and cheese contain B1, B2 and B12, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Dietary fiber (when whole‑grain dough is used)
items.content: If whole‑grain flour is used, the croissant can contribute dietary fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The layered butter and cheese make the croissant calorie‑dense, so it should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Butter and cheese increase saturated fat levels, which may affect cholesterol if consumed excessively.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese contains lactose; people with intolerance should choose lactose‑free cheese or avoid the product.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk or cheese should avoid cheese croissants to prevent reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheese croissants are best enjoyed hot, straight from the oven, when the cheese is still stretchy. They can be eaten as a snack, sliced for sandwiches, or added to salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store croissants in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Reheat in the oven before serving to restore crispness.
